title: Jamming with Tatum in Val's in the Alley
summary: Roy recalls Tatum, Lannie Scott, and the jam sessions and broadcasts of the Cotton Pickers days.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Did Art Tatum hang out with you guys, too, when you played?
Not then, no. We used to hang out together when I was with the Cotton Pickers. We played a ...(?)., but I think I told you about that.
We just touched on it, but didn't really talk much about it.

Well, I mean, he was working in the club, the Club Alabam, I think it was called -- him and Lannie Scott. Remember Lannie Scott? That was the weirdest thing. As long as Lannie Scott... See, Art had a room where he played when he was younger called the Blue Room, you know, and Lannie worked with Hardnott's(?) band. He had the band that played on Saturday. As long as Art was there, Lannie played marvelous. Man, he had a real thing with Art, you know -- up to a point. As soon as Art went away, then he didn't sound that way. He couldn't like get it together, you know.

And we used to wait on him, me and my brother and Clyde and Prince Robinson... And I sure wish they had tape recorders in those days, because we played some...we used to get some fabulous, fabulous things going in there, in that Val's In The Alley, you know. Then when we finished, we'd all go down to the diners, they had a little diner there, and Art would spring for the food, you know -- because we was seein' hard times!

I used to go with him on his broadcast, too. They had a big grand. I'd stay down there with him. I loved it, two weeks riding a cab, and when somebody would blow a horn they would start arguing what note it was. And I'd have to get my horn out to prove they were right, whoever had guessed (?).
